mechanicalChecks.countMethod: Strip HTML comments, Markdown link targets and Markdown markers, then remove whitespace; retain visible punctuation.

claimAudit.method: Every visitor-facing assertion was checked section by section against the authorized source pack, research card and writing plan, and classified as sourced fact, supplied visual observation or bounded editorial inference.

sectionResults.evidence: Artist and German label, circa 1908 date, tempera/canvas, Founding Collection identity, accession number boundary and dated On View status are supported.
Woman, snake, dark field, gold frame and allegorical sin/temptation range are supplied observations or bounded synthesis; no psychology or named biblical figure is asserted.

Frontal gaze, snake over the shoulders, bright eyes, dark field, cropped torso and architectural gold frame remain within the supplied observation boundary; the encounter with the viewer is presented as an effect of composition.
Most claims are supported, but two comparative visual rankings are not independently substantiated by the allowed textual evidence.
Near-black background, narrow vertical format, torso cut by darkness, horizontal snake and architectural frame are supplied observations; spatial pressure is a traceable editorial inference.

Multiple versions between 1891 and 1912, small compositional changes, circa 1908 late version, tempera/canvas, recurring motif and Symbolist placement are supported. The text does not claim a precise count or definite motive.

The 1893 Neue Pinakothek comparator, shared core, stated differences, medium-low rarity, mature career position and Frye collection role match the research evidence and stay within the 72-point boundary.
The six checks and final eye-to-eye-to-frame route return to supplied visual features; the concluding meaning is clearly a viewing judgment rather than an asserted historical fact.
Version/date/count uncertainty, allegorical range, unnamed figure, unknown psychology and mutable display status are stated accurately; all three supplied visitor sources are linked.

narrativeReview.coreQuestion: Why can a woman, a snake and two bright pairs of eyes turn sin into pressure faced by the viewer?

quickDeepIndependence.evidence: The quick layer supplies a complete viewing route and provisional answer; the deep layer adds spatial mechanism, motif recurrence, career placement and the nearest comparator.

cardQuickIndependence.evidence: The card's shared frontal gaze plus the exact body/snake/darkness/gold-frame bundle is a compressed rephrasing of the quick layer's central answer, rather than an independently conceived click reason.

significanceReview.label: 重要藏品

artisticAchievement.evidence: Narrow format, two eye highlights, darkness, bodily cropping and architectural frame are tied to concrete compositional control.

artHistoricalPosition.evidence: The work is placed within Stuck's successful, repeatedly worked Symbolist Sin motif without claiming first-version or unique status.

historicalCulturalValue.evidence: The plan assigns a bounded medium value to Symbolist treatments of sin, temptation and eroticized bodies and explicitly avoids treating the work as evidence of a specific historical event.

rarityAndIrreplaceability.evidence: Multiple 1891-1912 versions and the 1893 comparator make rarity medium-low; the core motif is substitutable, while the Frye version retains only version-specific and in-museum value.

museumCollectionPosition.evidence: The work is specifically identified as Frye's anchor for Stuck and Munich Symbolism.

significanceReview.artistCareerPosition: PASS — a mature later repetition of a successful motif, not a first or unique version.

nearestComparator.object: Neue Pinakothek, Franz von Stuck, 1893, Die Sünde
nearestComparator.sharedCore: narrow vertical format, dark background, snake across the shoulders and frontal gaze
nearestComparator.differences: date, tempera/canvas medium, specific tonality and architectural frame
nearestComparator.quantityBoundary: multiple versions are confirmed for 1891-1912; exact total remains unknown
nearestComparator.nonSubstitutabilityBoundary: The comparator can substitute for the motif's core art-historical value. This version remains non-substitutable only as the specific Frye object, its frame/tonality/material effect and its role in Frye's collection narrative.

significanceReview.frye72Boundary: PASS — no rare-treasure, world-class, unique, special-trip or itinerary-determining inflation appears.

workSpecificReview.evidence: The core question, headings, comparison, six details and final action depend on this work's paired eyes, shoulder-crossing snake, narrow dark field, gold architectural frame, circa 1908 late-version status and 1893 comparator; they cannot be transferred unchanged to another work.

productionLanguageScan.allowedEvidenceBoundaryLanguage: The exact-version-count limit and dated mutable On View status are visitor-relevant evidence boundaries, not internal production language.

dimensions.evidence: “画面最强的地方，是两道凝视同时逼近” immediately establishes a work-specific tension rather than an encyclopedia opening.
The draft connects paired gaze to allegory, darkness/frame to pressure, and multiple versions to both career position and reduced rarity.
Stuck's repeated reworking and adjustment of the motif is intelligible as artistic action, but the evidence does not support a fuller account of motive or decision.
The 1893 comparator changes the answer from apparent singularity to mature but substitutable motif value, then relocates the strongest claim to Frye's collection narrative.
The argument repeatedly returns to the two eyes, snake, shoulder line, cropped torso, narrow format and architectural frame.
The overall explanation is followable, but several compressed abstract collocations fail a natural continuous read-aloud test.
The ending gives the specific eye-to-snake-to-shoulders-to-frame action and changes the title from a label into a three-way viewing relation.
